what: Finding 055. Two implementations return a date when BYSETPOS selects the nth member of a set with fewer than n members, where the correct result is the empty set. These are PROBES, not corpus cases: they carry no score and nothing in conformance/RESULTS.md's tables depends on them. Validated by src/validity.py (rule 45).

rrulejs.claim: an out-of-range NEGATIVE BYSETPOS is clamped to the first element of the set; positive out-of-range is correct
rrulejs.corpus_case_reaching_this: c29dd0b92b8f (BYSETPOS=-2), the only case of this shape in the scored corpus
rrulejs.lineage_note: dateutil (upstream) and rust-rrule (downstream port of rrule.js) both correct; rule 24 collapses the three into one vote and they disagree here

libical.claim: exhausting ICAL_LIMIT_RECURRENCE_SEARCH is not a path that returns icaltime_null_time(); icalrecur_iterator_next falls through to `return impl->last` and hands back the date the search had reached

builds.3.0.20 (system): BYSETPOS ignored entirely at WEEKLY; a full expansion is returned

prior_art.795/944/21/67: closed, BYSETPOS ignored or partly implemented; none concerns an unsatisfiable selection
prior_art.1156/1279: the stall counter (time standing still / infinite loop in next_unit); a different exit than the budget
prior_art.1374: this repository's own report, opened 2026-09-08, fixed by PR #1387 on 2026-09-10

caveats: The libical probes are compiled directly against the library, not run through conformance/adapters/c/libical_adapter (rule 25).
The 958-year and 1917-year steps are arithmetic consistent with a 100000-iteration budget, not measurements of the iteration count.
The libical mechanism is read from source at scratch/libical checkout 4edd39a3 and confirmed by the budget-scaling experiment; it was not stepped through in a debugger.
Neither defect has been reported upstream; external reporting is paused for this repository.
